Parallax

A background image that moves slower than the page.

Parallax moves a background image at a different speed from the foreground as you scroll. The image lives in a parallax-container; the plugin is on the inner .parallax.

AutoInit() starts every .parallax except those marked no-autoinit. There must be an <img> inside. Without one, init logs an error and returns. 

<div class="parallax-container">
  <div class="parallax">
    <img src="images/parallax1.jpg" alt="A mountain lake">
  </div>
</div>

Use an image taller than the container. The plugin translates the leftover height as you scroll; a short image has nothing to move.

Initialization

The IIFE bundle exposes RoutePlate.Parallax. Call init yourself when you need options other than the defaults, or let RoutePlate.AutoInit() start every .parallax. 

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('.parallax');
  const instances = RoutePlate.Parallax.init(elems, {
    // specify options here
  });
});

Per-instance options can also be passed through AutoInit:

RoutePlate.AutoInit(document.body, {
  Parallax: { responsiveThreshold: 992 }
});

Options

Name Type Default Description
responsiveThreshold Number 0 Minimum viewport width, in pixels, at which the image starts moving. Below this width the transform is cleared.

Methods

All methods are called on the plugin instance. You can get the instance like this: 
const instance = RoutePlate.Parallax.getInstance(elem);
.destroy();

Destroy the plugin instance, clear the image transform, and tear down its event handlers. The last remaining instance also removes the shared scroll and resize listeners. 

instance.destroy();

Properties

Name Type Description
el Element The DOM element the plugin was initialized with.
options Object The options the instance was initialized with.

Customization

The container height is how much of the image you see. The framework default is 500px. Override it on the container. 

.parallax-container {
  height: 300px;
}
